summary: Sawyer County, WI tower listed by the FFLA as gone at 45.94618, -90.77030; not among the five Sawyer towers the DNR named in 2016; no source describes the site today.

evidence.quote: Seventy-two fire towers (mostly in Northern Wisconsin) used by the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (DNR), including five in Sawyer County, will be taken out of service in 2016

evidence.supports: the five Sawyer County towers named in the article were Hayward, Sand Lake, Pipestone, Swayne and Connors Lake, not Brunet
evidence.quote: Towers in Sawyer County include Hayward, located south of Hayward; another in the Town of Sand Lake; one in the middle of the county, Pipestone; and two in the lower half of the county: Swayne, between the villages of Radisson and Winter, and Connors Lake on the border of Price County.

sources.title: DNR will discontinue fire towers in 2016

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence. The Forest Lookouts Brunet page has only the heading and 'Wisconsin - Sawyer County' in the cached copy, so there is no build date, design, builder or staffing. The Sawyer County Record article names five Sawyer County DNR towers; Brunet is not among them, which suggests it was not on the DNR's Sawyer list in 2016, but the article does not say who owned Brunet or when it came down, so the story states only the absence. Statewide timing conflicts: the Sawyer County Record says the 72 towers 'will be taken out of service in 2016', while the WJFW article 'Connecting the dots' says the 72 towers were decommissioned in 2015. The story uses the 2016 wording and does not attribute Brunet's fate to that program. The OSM node 353893411 and data/sources/osm.json label the point 'standing', which is only map presence and conflicts with FFLA 'Gone'; not used. The anyplaceamerica listing (GNIS 1581183) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Access and visit fields omitted because no source describes them.
